topic: Beyond the Flatland: Solving Geometry Puzzles with Dimensional Shifts
target_audience: High school students and curious learners with a basic understanding of geometry

sections.title: The Boundary Constraint: Why Dimensions Matter
lecture_lines: Some geometry problems seem impossible within their own dimension.
Imagine an ant trapped inside a simple 2D circle.
In 3D, we can easily step over this boundary.
animations: Display a 2D ant icon inside a white #FFFFFF circle.
The ant moves against the circle boundary which flashes red #FF0000.
The camera perspective shifts as the ant is lifted over the boundary.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The N+1 Foundation
lecture_lines: Let's build up from zero dimensions.
A point extends into a one-dimensional line.
The line expands into a two-dimensional square.
Adding depth creates a three-dimensional cube.
We can unfold 3D objects into 2D nets.
animations: Show a yellow #FFFF00 3D cube.
Unfold the cube into a 2D cross-shaped net.
Draw a red #FF0000 path across the flat net.

sections.title: Puzzle 1: The Shortest Path (3D to 2D Shift)
lecture_lines: A spider wants the shortest path to a fly.
Navigating a 3D room makes the path look complex.
We can flatten the room into a single 2D plane.
On this flat map, the shortest path is a line.
This 2D shift reveals the hidden hypotenuse path.
animations: Show a 3D rectangular box in grey #808080 with dots for spider and fly.
A dashed pink #FF00FF line shows the spider's path across two walls.
The box walls unfold to form a flat 2D plane.
The spider and fly dots are now positioned on the flat plane.
A solid green #00FF00 line connects the dots, showing the shortest path.

sections.title: Puzzle 2: The Impossible Knot (2D to 3D Shift)
lecture_lines: Linked rings appear fused in two dimensions.
They cannot be separated without breaking.
Adding a Z-axis provides a new direction.
We lift one ring into the third dimension.
This extra degree of freedom separates the rings.
animations: Show two overlapping 2D rings, white #FFFFFF and blue #0000FF.
The overlap points flash red #FF0000 to show "stuck."
Introduce a green #00FF00 arrow for the Z-axis depth.
Lift the blue ring along the Z-axis.
Move the rings apart, resolving the intersection.

sections.title: The Fourth Dimension: Conceptual Projection
lecture_lines: A 3D cube casts a flat, 2D shadow.
Similarly, 4D objects project into our 3D space.
We study these shadows to understand higher dimensions.
animations: Rotate a yellow #FFFF00 cube casting a 2D grey #808080 shadow.
Introduce a cyan #00FFFF Tesseract 3D projection.
Rotate the Tesseract to morph its 3D projection.
Flash the vertices of the Tesseract in white #FFFFFF.
An 'impossible' 3D knot untangles using 4D logic.

sections.title: Summary: The Dimensional Toolkit
lecture_lines: Use dimensional reduction to simplify paths and distances.
Use dimensional expansion to bypass seemingly solid obstacles.
When stuck, ask if you are in the right dimension.
animations: Icons for 'Reduction' and 'Expansion' appear on a split screen.
A white #FFFFFF 2D maze appears with a character dot.
The dot scales up and 'jumps' over walls to the exit.
